prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: A fairer, greener UK built on urgent climate action, well-funded public services, reduced inequality, and stronger democracy.

Health and care
- Restore a fully public NHS; oppose privatisation. Extra NHS revenue funding rising from £8bn (year one) to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Faster GP access, universal NHS dentistry with £3bn/yr by 2030, mental health parity, school counsellors, assisted dying with safeguards, end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care, £20bn/yr investment; better pay/careers for carers; children’s social care +£3bn; disability benefits +5%.

Homes and communities
- Build 150,000 new social homes a year; end Right to Buy; rent controls via councils; end Section 21 evictions.
- Retrofit/insulation drive: £29bn for homes over 5 years (toward EPC B), £9bn low‑carbon heating, £7bn overheating adaptation; Passivhaus-standard new builds, solar and heat pumps mandated; planning reform to deliver services and protect green spaces.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; introduce a rising carbon tax (£120/t to £500/t within 10 years). Wind to provide ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035: 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar. Back community energy; remove barriers to local supply. Oppose new nuclear; phase out existing.

Economy and tax
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr (power, retrofit, rail, active travel, water/sewage, industry). Bring rail, water and Big 5 retail energy companies into public ownership. Regional mutual banks; SME decarbonisation grants; +£30bn for R&D over 5 years. Circular economy, right to repair, 10‑year warranties.
- Fairer taxes: Wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align capital gains and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; property tax reforms toward Land Value Tax; stronger windfall taxes; carbon tax. Raise £50–70bn/yr (personal), up to £80bn/yr from carbon by end of parliament. Borrow to invest; reject restrictive fiscal rules.

Work and welfare
- Repeal anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage (support for SMEs); 10:1 pay ratios; full rights from day one; protect gig workers; move toward four‑day week.
- Raise Universal Credit/legacy benefits by £40/week; scrap five‑week wait and two‑child cap; carers’ allowance +10%; protect pensions; long‑term Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% of land/sea by 2030; public ownership of water; Clean Air Act; expand Right to Roam. End factory farming and blood sports; Commission on Animal Protection.
- Food: Free school meals for all children; triple farm support to shift to nature-friendly farming, more UK horticulture, reduced pesticides.

Education
- Free, inclusive education: scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; £8bn for schools (incl. teacher pay), £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings; £5bn for SEND; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; expand Sure Start and childcare; invest in FE, lifelong learning, EMA.

Transport
- Public transport first: subsidies rising to £10bn/yr; £19bn over 5 years for upgrades and active travel; rail in public hands; free buses for under‑18s; £2.5bn/yr for cycling/walking; oppose new roads; road pricing; end sales of new petrol/diesel cars by 2027, phase out use by 2035; frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion, ban short domestic flights where rail <3 hours.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Fair Politics Act: proportional representation, repeal voter ID, party funding reform; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; defend HRA/ECHR; self‑ID for trans people; scrap protest-curbing laws.
- Migration: End hostile environment, safe routes, right to work for asylum seekers, abolish NRPF and 10‑year route, remove income thresholds for family visas; new Department of Migration; visa fees at cost; NHS access free.

Culture, digital, justice, foreign policy
- £5bn for local arts/sport; implement Leveson; cap media market share at 20%; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation.
- Policing/justice: rebuild trust, end routine stop-and-search and facial recognition; misogyny a hate crime; decriminalise sex work; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; invest to clear court backlogs and restore legal aid.
- Foreign policy: Support Ukraine; immediate permanent ceasefire in Israel–Gaza, recognise Palestine, end UK arms to Israel; aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; work toward rejoining EU (customs union first); sign TPNW, cancel Trident; reform NATO focus on defence, no‑first‑use.
